newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee to dip to 36.73 by July - Stanchart poll.
newsitem.headline: India rupee to dip to 36.73 by July - Stanchart poll.

text.p: The Indian rupee is expected to depreciate to 36.73 against the dollar by July 1997 from the current rate of 35.85, according to a poll of 100 top company treasurers conducted by Standard Chartered Bank.
"Treasurers see the rupee depreciating to 36.73 by July 1997," the bank said in a statement announcing the poll results.
"Export selling far forward may still be profitable."
The poll showed the dollar value at a mean of 36.03 rupees in one month, 36.35 in three months and 36.73 in six months.

"While large dollar outflows during 1997 on account of the redemption of India Development Bonds and the IMF loan repayment are known with certainty, uncertainty persists on the front of inflows," the bank said in a commentary on the poll.

"The expected increase in the oil import bill, unlikely portfolio investments and sluggish exports should weaken the rupee notwithstanding a buildup of reserves by the RBI (Reserve Bank of India)," it said.
It said the central bank is expected to allow the rupee to weaken gradually by 2.45 percent over the next six months.
"Thus, exporters should still take advantage of premia and receive forward," the bank commentary said.
The poll forecast forward dollar premia to remain flat at around 7.0 percent, strengthening the case for export sales.
It said companies with large unhedged positions demanding forward covers could cause forward premia to rise marginally.
A section of the polled treasurers believed that the rupee could dip beyond the 38.0 per dollar level over the next three to six months causing a marginal spurt, the bank said.
"However, current forward premia already being on the higher slope, do not reflect interest differentials and therefore should see flattening out beyond three months."
